God, Glorious in Majesty, said of the hypocrites: "They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts," and regarding some hypocrites, those who pretend to be guides to people, but when they come near — "Those who believe, when they meet those who believe, say 'We believe,' but when they go apart to their devils they say, 'We are with you; we were only mocking.' God will mock them and leave them to wander blindly in their transgression." And the Messenger, God's peace be upon him, said: "The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he promises, he breaks his promise; when he is trusted, he betrays; when he speaks, he lies." And in another narration: "And when he disputes, he acts wickedly." And he said: "I seek refuge in God from the hypocrite." And he said: "Two qualities never come together in a hypocrite: good intention and understanding of religion." And he said: "Whoever has two faces in this world will have two tongues of fire on the Day of Resurrection." And he said: "The most harmful of the learned is the hypocrite who betrays in this world and the next." And the Arab saying goes: "Indeed, one who is like paper and pen brings disgrace to the two-faced, and speech that is like paper takes revenge; and striking with the pen that turns is like a judge who leads religion astray." Ardabili says: "Whoever raises his head like a hypocrite, with a two-tongued face — make his face black as ink, and like a pen bent over five times — beat him." And the work of the hypocrite: God, Glorified and Exalted be He, mocks them, as He said: "Those who proceed in their hearts..."

The lowest of the ignoble is the envious heart — the tongue smooth and flattering, the heart full of pain.
To the wise man, the glory of the deluded one avails nothing — he who steps forth into the wilderness for worldly gain.
Let them be bound by that house whose end is slipping down; put it to use.
Striving and going without true meaning — like a flute whose desire is not fulfilled; so it was said.
He explained the reins of speech, saying: likewise it means these things — and he opened the way.
It was there, and the company of Jamsh and Khalid were there — near the mountains and valleys, and so they dispersed.
Their great ones reduced the mountains to level ground, and in speech we have reached the intimacy of the Jews.
The head of courage is like those who preceded, like lovers — and the heart, troubled, finds rest.
And when Khidr acted, it was as a warning to those who passed by — Mahmud stood against ignorance, therefore beware.
In excess and foolishness — listening to the voice of fancy, the thought was there, and so it wandered.
Improper desire is increased by the cup and by passion, and the meaning is: if one is generous, the reader is satisfied.
In excess of God one loses, and in neglect of the son there is no will — there is no escape from this.
Firdawsi says: "Time provides for everyone alike — as it is arranged, so comes the daily sustenance."
And the Arabs have a saying for this: delay belongs to time — and the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, peace be upon him, declared:
"Ignorance is death before death for its people, and their souls are trapped in darkness — know this."
The woman seeks knowledge without measure — and the Arabs say: "Do not come near."
Envy: one who covets and desires what belongs to others has brought ruin upon himself.
Those who seek protection through God — the Prophet, may God protect him — said concerning envy: it destroys the foundation.
Ordering it thus, God the Exalted has said: "And from the evil of the envier when he envies" — and the Prophet taught:
"O God, make me one who is envied and do not make me an envier" — for these reasons:
The worst and most base of things is envy; it destroys the one who envies while leaving the envied person unharmed.

Know that envy inflames however much you try to extinguish it. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Beware of envy, for envy devours good deeds just as fire devours wood." It has been said: the envious one finds no rest. Sheikh Sa'di says: We have no need to trouble you — we leave it to your own conscience. The best rebuke for a base person is that if he gains nothing from hardship, then what he speaks is in vain. In the Noble Word of God, the honor of its revelation came regarding the rabbis of the Jews — that people envied what God had given others from His grace. And Joseph said: The first sin of envy was the disobedience of God, for it was the sin of Iblis toward Adam, the first disobedience of God upon earth, and it was the envy of Adam's son toward his brother, when he killed him. In the words of the wise it is said: no envy came but from envy itself. It has been said: whoever is content with God's decree — envy shall not enter his heart, for whoever withholds food from others, envy enters him. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Be patient against the plotting of the envious, for if you are patient, God will suffice you against him, just as fire consumes fire — consuming all its fuel. If the envious one finds you firm, his envy breaks against his own heart and he gains nothing. As for arrogance: if one becomes arrogant, he falls like a drunkard without recovery, and excess beyond measure — the commanders and their like said: the most foolish is the deluded one, and the wisest of the wise sees that arrogance means lowliness. If one is base, ignoble, and of low character, and if he is shown kindness, he grows proud and is praised, then regrets it, and then reveals his evil nature. The wise have said: do not be drawn in — a generous gift cuts off what was, but once it is lost, it cannot be recovered. Its outwardness brings disgrace and its source is praised and satirized. A wise man said: Know that a person cannot be known in two years, but through speech one may know what does not benefit him.

He settled there, having received news through the intermediary, and set out in pursuit of that matter. Reason and religious law both call for staying in that place, because staying brings comfort to oneself and to others.
He departed from the path of deficiency and returned the trust, restoring things to their proper place and returning them to their rightful owners. In terms of both reason and tradition, he turned away from that matter and kept people alive — and in this meaning it is said:
The service of caring for dependents and family is something that no one wishes to bear. Everyone is always fearful and anxious, as it is said: "Whoever opposes the eighty..." — in another's path he spent and went out, and those bases of noble descent...
The matter reached such a point that through poor management and lack of principle it came to ruin. He sought and the matter reached the point where it had already been determined and decreed. It was possible that his own soul and the actions of others might move forward.
But if the matter arrived at its proper time and place, the covenant would be established and the bond of affection would remain. In this meaning it is said: "Therefore, the death of Moses the Prophet came to him in peace," and he asked of God, blessed and exalted: "Do not make me suffer among enemies, and do not make me of the company of the wrongdoers."
To know and understand this is itself sufficient for living well. One should learn from others and not cause harm — one who comes to those in the same situation and shares in their learning will increase. If one is in that state and the ignorant person gives no news, and the tongue adds more than needed — if they report something and the speaker does not speak with the tongue properly, and saying nothing is also not right — in this meaning it is said: "The ignorant one, if he speaks such words, strikes out."
So be silent, and follow the guidance of the teacher, and he will lead you correctly toward the right path. According to this principle and this meaning, one should take heed and set sail upon it.

Other than one's tongue, what right does one have to speak freely? And in the words of the reproachful poet it is said: "To replace base manners — what is oppression from your nature, O base one?" And in the words of the sages it is written: "Among the signs of ignorance is to impose on the undeserving, and to withhold from one who is entitled — this is oppression."

Oppression: When one has acted unjustly toward one who did not deserve it, and seeks the means of livelihood wrongfully — just as one who digs at the chest of another such person is himself an oppressor, as the saying goes: "Among them is one who wrongs his own soul," and for the sake of preventing hunger and destitution, and reaching the possessions of the greedy — the oppressor always has abundant wealth, while the oppressed has little capital, and the just person is moderate in condition. And in the Noble Word it is said: "Do not incline toward those who have done wrong, lest the Fire touch you," and "You have no protector besides God, nor will you be helped." And God Most High says: "Verily the curse of God is upon the oppressors," and it is said that oppression is darkness. And it is said: "Beware the supplication of the oppressed, for it is not veiled," and among the counsels to the believers: "Do not oppress, and what was established — for the oppressor his punishment will reach him." The oppressor's name is blighted, and God's eye is upon him. And in the words of the Arabs it is said: "Oppression cuts off lives and prevents growth." And Khusraw Anushirvan said: "Oppression brings humiliation to the oppressed and to the oppressor alike," and it was said: "We have lost children, turned away relatives and brothers." Sheikh Sa'di, in the chapter on the oppressor, says: "The oppressor is gone and the unjust seat remains," the just man has passed and his good name endures in deeds — "Bitterness and sweetness, ugliness and beauty have all passed away; only the record of the oppressor and tyrant remains." In dealing with us by wealth it has passed — Oppression: it was by his hand that he acted unjustly, the mighty was humiliated by him, and now that account is false, and harmful to the body of the worshiper. God Most High says: "O you who believe, avoid much suspicion, for indeed some suspicion..."

And the word of the Almighty: "Conjecture avails nothing against the truth," and the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Beware of conjecture, for conjecture is the most lying of speech." Hawdh ibn Sandal was wicked and stingy.

Carrying Hawdh and its qualities — from the number of Hawdh, made known by the son of Malkim from Ajil, Shamar — Nanak says: "O you who are self-deceived, you who look only at yourself, you who see Hawdh" — whatever person speaks thus, he is far from good manners.

The Prophet said: "The example of a king whose shaykh is obeyed while he himself is forsaken, and the faults of the soul [are ignored]." And he said: "Truly the loneliness of the solitary one is better than bad companionship," and old age and frequenting evil deeds — "From the moment God granted this," he pointed out — a person who is preoccupied with the faults of others and in his own character does not reflect — this is something strange among people of reason.

That is to say: when appearance and inner character are brought together, the one who is self-deceived — he said: "Arrogance makes life unpleasant. Arrogance makes life unpleasant." Justice — my master — established this: relying on the great for support and employing it in matters of rank and status is something that no wise person has praised.

The Prophet said: "Every treacherous person will have a banner raised on the Day of Resurrection, identifying him by his treachery." The Commander of the Faithful Ali said: "Loyalty belongs to the people of excuse in the sight of God, but for the people of treachery, God has prepared punishment." And in noble speech it is established: the one who chooses vanity and describes and likens — one should look upon him with great discernment.

And over others: one should guard one's virtue and maintain order in all affairs. For others who are unable to restrain themselves — anger and wrath — one should suppress it, and be measured. He reached a place where, thinking carefully and with proper conduct, he would be guided aright.

It records from the Prophet, peace be upon him, that "Anger is from Satan, and Satan is from fire, and fire is extinguished by water, so when one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution." And it is said: Anger is fire, and Satan is fire, so whoever extinguishes the fire of anger is protected from the fire of Satan.

And it is said: Anger comes from fire, so suppress it and love for you to be sober. If one is standing, let him sit, and if one is sitting, let him lie down. The condition of backbiting among people is described as follows: that is, if some old saying reaches someone in this manner, this attribute is also read otherwise — meaning that God, Exalted and Glorified, does not overlook the unseen matters that are hidden from the people. It is written in the book: Do not display faults except to the Knower of the Unseen. And it is said: Whoever conceals the faults of others upon himself, God will conceal his faults in this world and the next. And in the hadith, from the Prophet, peace be upon him: Sin — and backbiting is that — the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Do you know what backbiting is?" It was said: What do you say, O Messenger? He said: "If what you say about your brother is true, then you have backbitten him, and if it is not in him, then you have slandered him." And it is said that he who complains about his brother in seeking justice — it is then a right upon God Almighty.

Lying: Lying is one of the traits that causes harm, and those who fall into lying lose honor and dignity. The purpose of mentioning it is as a lesson. And lying corrupts the human species. God Almighty says: "Lying is invented only by those who do not believe in the signs of God, and those are the liars." And in the hadith, from the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire." And he, peace be upon him, said: "Woe to him who lies to make people laugh." And he said: "Avoid lying."

Lying

Lying — and even if one sees in it salvation, in it is in fact destruction. Whoever lies deliberately has secured for himself a place in the Fire. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was asked: "Beware of lying!" — for it is one of the gates of the Fire. It is said: "Is a believer a fornicator?" He said: "Yes." It was said: "Is a believer a polytheist?" He said: "No." And the Commander of the Faithful Ali (peace be upon him) said: "Lying degrades men." And a wise man said: "Sometimes falsehood and the dead are alike, for the virtue of truth is that it speaks; and when the dead man speaks through his words, he has prolonged his life." And 'Abdullah Mubarak said: "The first punishment of the liar is that his truthfulness is rejected." And it is said: "Lying is not recognized for it brings no credibility." It is also said: "Lying is the root of all evil and the foundation of all blame." In the book of Mansur it is stated: "Lying is companion to all vice." Lying — deception, betrayal, and fraud — is all blameworthy. And it is said regarding poetic excellence: "The finest of poetry is its most fictional." Sheikh Sa'di says: "A useful white lie is better than a sedition-stirring truth." — Showing something that does not exist outwardly leads only to inner harm, and this quality breeds conflict. As the Almighty says: "Shun false speech" — and backbiting. A Chinese poet has said: "From whispering, no good comes; heed this." These vices were not sought even by the wretched. And in the noble word, the sword strikes — "their provision is but the goods of this world" — and the meaning is: do not let them have any portion. And it is reported from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him): "Do not backbite." It appears in the Manshur: "Backbiting is a killing sword." And in the words of the wise it is said: "Backbiting is the sword of time, the serpent of high places, and the destroyer of esteem."

The explanation, alongside its counterpart, and at the shores of the religion and the world:
God revealed to Moses (upon him be peace): "In a land, there are wealthy men who do not listen to those who bring joy, while they are upon the earth." So Moses said, "O Lord, guide me to the hajj of Huzjabr." He replied, "O Moses, for every blessing—" and as for the Khwaja himself, in his own affairs, in the matters of the land and its affairs, neither the noble nor the elder nor the younger of his own has known restraint or measure. As an explanation for the limbs prepared to be offered, "Now to the dye," —and let them remember greed and avarice, covetousness and desire for more. Beyond what is necessary, and acquiring more than needed without accomplishing what is proper, and the description of virtue is that it is not [to go] to extremes, and worship and the pursuit of knowledge—the greedy and impatient are described. These are virtues. Second: one who holds this quality in worldly affairs—it is transmitted in the traditions from the Messenger, peace be upon him: "If the son of Adam had two valleys of gold, he would wish for a third, and nothing fills the belly of Adam except the earth." And it is said: "O God, I seek refuge with You from greed that leads me to a greed other than provision," and Walid ibn Abd al-Muttalib—may God reward him—and Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "One who grazes today is not to be trusted," and do not let greed arise. As it is said: "Every son of Adam seeks, by my life, provision, and the greedy one is bound and tied." And the Commander of the Faithful, Ali (peace be upon him), said: "I fear for you two things: following desire and the length of hope, for following desire turns one away from the truth, and the length of hope causes one to forget the hereafter." Firdausi says: "Greed is worshipped—seek not degradation."

Bakri refuted those two and said that Jalal al-Din ibn Barzi was bad, and chanted a charm over him.
I heard by way of news: do not busy yourself with your husband's affairs; the pure-hearted woman is old.
As long as hypocrisy is in a person's nature, going astray and turning away, he will be in decline from the start.
Do not listen: the great ones said that greed is bad; keep away from greed, for greed brings ruin to you.
Learning nothing from the wise, you have fled away from them; go far from the people of ambition and worldly acquisition.
Repentance of Adam and the prophets: seek virtue and generosity; hear the long counsel.
Al-Hasan al-Basri said: the best jihad is the jihad against one's own desires, and you are among those who know this.
And in the speech of the wise it is said: greed is the foundation of corruption in religion and the source of disgrace.
Those seized by greed become weakened in spirit; those who sit among the greedy will be ensnared.
Al-Abbasi said: whoever occupies himself excessively in the pursuit of wealth will be burdened by that wealth.
A wise man gave counsel to his children: do not be covetous, for covetousness leads to further covetousness.
The burden of wealth increases, and the great ones have said: desire leads to more desire. And in the book of ethics,
Al-Nasiri said: greed is in the nature of most people; deception is the source of cunning and appearances.
One of them related that he came and brought people to the right path, and those far away drew near.
The virtuous and the righteous and the devout and their families and others found meaning in this.
The deceptions of God are recorded in the Book, and by this sign
He called himself among the possessors of wealth and devoted himself to following the Messenger of God, peace be upon him.
He kept this and profited from deception, making his affairs succeed.
He was a captain who, by means of this, made others sour and turned them away, keeping them under his authority.
Certainly, by the worker of corruption he came to those whose right and whose true path was blocked, so they could not reach their goal.
To the people of the way, the Messenger came to them, and from those present the choice was made.

A poet says: "One who acts badly and praises good deeds, yet remains mired in wrongdoing — listen, you have not heard the melody of those who repay kindness, for harshness is like playing with thorns." Indeed, the cunning of women is known to surpass that of men, and in truth the cunning of women is immense. God the Exalted says: "Indeed your cunning is great," and in the commentary on the cunning of women there are books, and various passages taken from Zahra, regarding the cunning of women of that kind, whose nature has been described. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said regarding those who accompany companions in Hell, and in the ethics of Nasiri it is said: That which is predominant — jest and humor — leads to the diminishment of words and actions and reduces one's standing. Its meaning was that when humor is refined and gentle, it has been recorded as such, and our noble Prophet, peace be upon him, used to associate with souls and it has been manifested many times in the books of history, and based on this, the most eloquent and refined speech is that — though some engage in jest in the view of people, this leads to harm, to bad and impure people. In Persian, the Commander of the Faithful Ali, peace be upon him, said: "Seek success through it, for I was not created for them nor for the three except for this." In the book Nuṣūr al-Ḥakīm: "Jest with trivial people is like feeding fire with firewood," and in the dictionary it is marked thus. It is said: "Do not play with a child or a slave," as the noble one has warned, for it leads to the loss of religious and worldly standing, of wealth, honor and other things, reducing and diminishing them. And the best of people are those who attain the peace of the soul, and the noblest of them are those with the power of angelic souls. That is, from the tranquil soul which they sought, and the animal soul is what is called the blaming soul.

The power called the animal soul (nafs bahīmī) is that which desires what it desires, and the wise say this is the animal self. The lordly soul (nafs malakī) possesses generosity and good conduct, while the animal soul, though it lacks innate good conduct, is nevertheless capable of being trained and disciplined. The animal soul is bestial and brutish in nature, and in the existence of the animal soul, the dominance of that soul leads to deviation and corruption and away from the right path. But in the existence of the lordly soul, seekers of truth and those who repel falsehood are guides to truth. Some philosophers call it the rational soul (nafs nāṭiqa), while some call it intellect and meaning. The rational soul is a substance that, however it assumes a form, manifests a quality in each form — it is not limited in number. It receives divine inspirations and intimate communications, and it attains intimacy. Among its stations is that it may descend to the level of cattle. Our Prophet — may God's blessings and peace be upon him — said: The divine pen separates souls to bring humanity from ignorance and misguidance toward religion and the straight path of the holy law. And noble souls adorn people with various virtues, erasing every kind of vice, so that souls gain strength, sharpness, and swiftness of discernment. This is confirmed for the purpose of proving and verifying the miracles of the revealed law. The scattered souls of people follow and comply with these noble souls and continue to do so. Salvation consists in this: that the soul be distinguished from the generality of people in truth, with genuine virtues and absence of vices. The souls of the prophets who are messengers are most numerous in this, and the souls of the Prophets of Firm Resolve (ūlū al-ʿazm) surpass those of ordinary messengers; and the soul of the greatest of them is complete and perfected beyond all — it is impossible and inconceivable to describe it fully — and his commanding power was such that by his sign ships could sail.

Just as one takes [poison] from snakes and [uses it so that] the mountain spirit comes between the two and replaces [harm with benefit] — and in the noble Qur'an there is mention of this: "He does not speak from desire, it is naught but a revelation revealed" — know that with all these qualities and faculties, and with all these virtues, they [the prophets] are capable of manifesting miracles outwardly whenever necessary, in accordance with truth, and whatever proceeds from the divine will. This is the meaning of "He does not speak from whim, it is only revelation" — and this confirms what Sheikh Sa'di said:

Someone asked: "How did you become so learned? For you are wiser than the sages of the age."
He said: "Whatever I smelled, I caught the scent of; I fell into the well of self-abandonment."
"Our work is like lightning — one moment it is here, another moment gone. At one instant I am at the highest heaven, at another I am grasping with my fist at the ground. If the secret of both worlds were on my lips, I would scatter it to the winds."

The souls of the saints — may God's pleasure be upon them all — are lower in rank than the souls of the prophets, and their miracles [karamat], though not obligatory signs, are nonetheless manifested by them at appropriate times for the benefit of others. There are many examples of this: the walking on water, the traversing of dry land, and other such things. These are the commands of God the Most High, and this is the meaning of "Islam encompasses all of this." These are the stations of the prophets. Sheikh Abdullah Ansari said it well:

"No one walks on water until a person of pure heart [comes forth] — no one becomes a master until someone else [guides them]."

"O wayfarer, if you fly through the air, know that going astray is still possible."

As for the sages, they too are at times capable of manifesting wonders, and the wisdom behind this is that the souls of the sages are, in their perspicacity, subtler than the souls of the saints, and hence the inspiration [ilham] that touches them is because the hearts of the sages are made pure and clear in all things manifest.

He makes manifest, and by way of analogy, from the name of the dead he gives news — their method is called "qiyas." O people, do not be deceived by this; it occurs and coincides with news by chance. And "Verily in that is a sign for the believers," meaning for those of discernment. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Beware of the intuition of the believer," and God Almighty said: "I have servants who judge people by their appearance," and he also said: "Beware the intuition of the believer, for he sees by the light of God." Such intuition is partly natural and partly acquired — the greater part comes from practice and experience, and partly it remains from experience alone.

Among the Greeks, the philosophers and sages, and among the people of Iran, physiognomy was known. The people of Islam too have not neglected this matter in religion, and there are those who practice the art of physiognomy. They applied it in various matters and some have spoken of its rules. The people of physiognomy also drew conclusions from the voices of men, the cries of birds and animals and the like. For example, when they were once on the road in a city they heard a voice saying: "O commander, accept our surrender!" and they turned back. Someone said: "We have called out our surrender," and they said: "May God lead us" — so they reached the city of Medina in safety, gained their reward, and God saved them.

The souls of the masters of physiognomy are more refined than the souls of ordinary men, and they are of two kinds: one is the physiognomy of the human form, and the other is the physiognomy of the resurrection — a guide to the signs of the Day of Judgment. This is established among the Arabs and is particularly associated with the tribe of Banu Mudlij, who are known for it, and they have great expertise in it. The art of physiognomy is a vast science, and those in the West who are called "al-sinān" are wondrously skilled in this matter, and those who are masters of this meaning among them are most knowledgeable, so that they discern from marks on men below...

Young and old come from land and sea, returning from their homeland, and the meaning of this is that the noblest of them settle here. The basis of the army is this, and the reason for both is the familiarity with that place and the clarity of mind that results. Knowledge of physiognomy is thereby confirmed, and by religious custom everything is reliable. The sinful and lowly souls are ruined; souls that have preceded us in discipline, through repeated practice, have attained purity in governance and the purity of their nature, so that imagination and noble thoughts prevail. This shows that whatever happens in accordance with events, they adapt to it. Their generosity and the Brahmins of India and others like them, the noble ones, the perfected ones — from the purity of the rational soul, things are set right; through repeated effort and spiritual discipline, clarity is achieved, and those who have attained purity of soul through striving and spiritual exercise come to know and comprehend these meanings. These things are possible in terms of cause and effect, and in relation to places and states, God has established that this dwelling is for pure souls. The souls described as mixed — if the soul is not pure, it will fall into the trap described; if it is made turbid, it will be led astray, and if the soul remains polluted, the character of the people will be harmed. God Almighty wished for things to appear in such a form, and thus it comes about. In Iran and India there are mountains, herbs, and plants. Their essence rises and nourishes the kingdom, and from them herbs of a certain quality grow in India. In that island there are great and ancient peoples, of tall stature, with large veins and deep roots. They came there, and in response to that, the messenger of the kingdom arrived.

A few who were companions went forth and found a tree that was like a shining star; it sent forth branches and leaves like gleaming lightning. Its roots were established and firm, its benefits abiding in the world — blessed in the world. The tree of the wise stretched toward the heavens and was made firm and strong. Year after year it grew fresh and young, and its saplings spread their reach endlessly like a trunk spreading wide. The gardeners came and tended it, and the gardeners drew from it the essence of that creature. They drew near it with care and admiration, and its beauty was like the noble palm tree of Arabia. The greatness and firmness of it was like the evergreen cypress of the kingdom, and the fragrance of oud was upon it. A burning passed through the green of the tree; they saw its leaves turn dark, and with garments of fortune they were overwhelmed. In no way could they breach its fortress; they set their hearts firmly and would not retreat. Here and there they strove, and so-and-so came forth in ignorance. A great wind came upon it and that great tree served as a pen, and a messenger was sent. On behalf of India a reply was sought; the wise of India spoke thus of its form. The reply came back from the messenger; it came again, and the reply was given: the king is among the wise. The interpretation of this riddle reached India: those who are like diamonds are advisors and counselors. In kingship and among the nobles, counsel and loyalty are doubled, and the aspiration of care and magnanimity: if the great king listens with satisfaction to all classes, and strives in justice and righteousness, then by God's grace the stability of the realm will be maintained and its affairs will be well ordered. But if the rulers are heedless of the oppression of the people and attend not to the truth, then oppression and enmity will increase, and all efforts will be turned toward the pen of destruction, and ruin will follow.

Although it soon took form, the tradition counted but a few,
Upon the pen they planted such a tree with humility, the pen remained, and whatever came of it,
The Creator of the kingdom gave it permanence, and quickly its fire was kept alight,
And it is right that its crookedness and confusion be transferred, and its knots untied from ignorance,
If one balances within oneself the essence of love and poetry, and fairness is gathered, purity emerges,
The soul that is perfectly pure and the perfectly pure soul is of great nobility and honor.
Old and new: the permanence of fortune endures, the hand of such affairs remains — Hova Atnak —
"No permanence" is the reverse of "fortune"; Glory be to God the Most High, Ruler of this age,
May He grant success and felicity, His exalted being — The Fourth Consideration:
Love and the seeking of the Divine Master is the perfection of the human soul and the manifestation of the intended purpose,
Since the outward and inward form of the existence of man, his qualities, traces and particulars,
Have been discussed in previous chapters — now from this meaning which
Has been put forth: the manifestation of the human is wondrous — "I was a hidden treasure and I wished
To be known, so I created creation in order to be known" — the realization of the goal and its establishment,
Has been affirmed and arranged properly, vast in scope, with the possibility of attaining knowledge —
And on the other side, in the unveiling, it is reckoned — God willing, with the agreement of the people of this sphere —
Through reliable proofs and clear demonstrations it is established that the human being is the noblest
Of all existing things, and in the ultimate purpose of creation it has been placed — "I created not creation for any purpose
Other than" — that noble essence and the intended goal from all things is the form and meaning of existence, meaning that
The purpose of the manifestation through this transient physical form is to reveal the qualities of the human spirit,
For the human being is complete and the purpose of his creation from the Lord of Majesty, free from annihilation and cessation.

Al-Askari says: You might wonder at this affair — how dominion is to be sought, and how greed consumes one. Listen to me: among all these, the command of both worlds transcends all. The servant has been humbled and set upon a path, compelled to follow it; sloth has come upon him through God's will. Inevitably, one forgets the self — but "God guides those who struggle in His path to His ways" — so seek and reflect. The meaning of the Water of Life — "Whoever knows himself" — shines amid the darknesses of existence. Observe how when you taste its sweetness and have truly recognized it, you will find your rank; it will reach your heart, and in your innermost being the truth of that will resound and you will remember it. Take on the form of one repentant, with purity of reason and wisdom of tongue, listening and moving and returning — until that sovereignty which no sovereignty can contain comes to be. Existence is made known: the nightingale sings of being, of simplicity, of rest and companionship; the very simplicity of existence draws near, desiring union, and hope is severed. Through this, unity and eternity are attained, and through the appearance of oneness and eternal priority and order, it is so — and existence returns, seeking that far-off grace. You seek the sun, the water of the house, and the sea of patience — consider this example: keep it in your sleeve. Whoever takes it as a burden will inevitably find himself halted. Your existence has been made aware, refined, and the knowledge of God Most High has been confirmed to you through Husayn ibn Mansur al-Hallaj, who said: "I sacrificed my crown, and became a seeker of the beloved, and I wished that the veil would be lifted from the heart of its riches — had not the light of intimacy risen over you, and had not the tradition come, you could not have risen beyond mere hearing of names." So do not follow in mere imitation: know yourself from within — I have heard this very name.

I was in existence from the time I came to know myself, until I went beyond myself and was brought back and came to know myself.
The people of the heart say in truth that this is why the lower world draws inward and becomes free and liberated.
The reason is that in the spiritual and physical realms, the acquisition of knowledge and benefits takes place.
And from the perspective of theoretical and intellectual inquiry, they sought knowledge; and in the lower world of animals and bodies,
completion is attained; and from the perspective of the higher, the rational self aspires, and the three souls — the tranquil soul (nafs-i mutma'inna),
the blaming soul (nafs-i lawwama), and the commanding soul (nafs-i ammara) — come to manifest in outward and inward faculties, appearing in actions.
The works arising from existence have been produced, and it is said that the tranquil soul has the quality of angelic and spiritual nature, while the commanding soul seeks the acquisition of pleasures,
and the attainment of animal pleasures and delights; and the blaming soul, from both sides, strives to maintain a balance — but whichever side grows stronger prevails, so that
whenever the tranquil state governs, the soul engages with the subtle realities of the spiritual world and progresses toward perfection;
and whenever the commanding soul takes hold and leads toward worldly desire, the soul loses its way and pursues the world;
and whenever the blaming soul is in a state of balance, it holds the soul from both sides, unable to strengthen either, and so the person
changes form and seeks different things at every moment. For this reason, the prophets and saints —
may God's pleasure be upon them — in whatever state they were, have been witnesses of God, as
the Messenger, when he looked inward at himself and at others, said: "I am not like any of you."
And when he looked at his outward self and at others, he said: "I was a prophet when Adam was still between water and clay."
And when he looked at the outward of himself and the inner of others, he said: "I am the son of Abraham."
"It has always been so from ancient times." And because of this, the spiritual world, whose qualities are of the merciful divine nature, is such that

The world echoes the afterlife — one who is lost in this world will be even more lost in the next, which has no end. Coming into this world is like water, and dwelling in it and departing from it is not within our choice. We were not sent here for the sake of it, but rather to be drawn toward salvation.

The master Sayyid al-Rasul, our Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever seeks what was not created for him, and seeks provision before its time — God has mercy on the one who remembers this world and calls it the abode of the believers, and God has called the unbeliever's comfort here a trial." And the Sheikh Abu Sa'id Abu al-Khayr said: "Tell them that this world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the unbeliever." Being in this world is a burden and incomprehensible, and from this judgment the Sheikh said — the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, declared: "Paradise has been made ready." This is evidence that the world was made ready as if for a day, and in relation to the next world it is like a drop.

And from this world nothing is to be grasped. As the hadith says: "The world compared to the afterlife is as nothing." So one must strive, for without knowing God, no harvest can be reaped. Even if one plants wheat, it will not yield without the reason of knowing God, which is obligatory for everyone. And knowing one's own self is also obligatory. If one does not do any of these, one will never reach anywhere near true knowledge, as it is said in the speech of the masters: "Know God as He truly deserves to be known," and the Prophet said: "I cannot enumerate Your praises upon You." The Exalted One said — meaning, one cannot fully do so — "Glory be to You, we have not known You as You truly deserve to be known, glory be to You, we have not worshipped You as You truly deserve to be worshipped." The word that must not be abandoned, the step that must be taken on this path — departing from and ceasing this worldly occupation is best. And the servant must be endowed with readiness, and persistently seeking, and somehow finding ecstatic presence.

The praise of none is more beneficial than the one who strives — all effort is wasted and the seeker will find nothing.
And if the sun were to stay in your breast, Adam the Chosen, the Elect of God, would be extinguished and undone.
Truly God chose Adam and Noah, and the family — He raised them and elevated their station on high.
And Noah achieved salvation, and We saved him and his family from the great affliction — this is the meaning of it —
For Abraham was clothed with the robe of intimate friendship: "And We took Abraham as a friend" — so understand this.
Moses was the first to whom the treasury was opened and God spoke to Moses directly — so drink of this cup.
And David was seated upon the throne of God's vicegerency: "O David, We have made you a vicegerent on earth" — dwell in this.
Solomon sat in the assembly wearing the crown of authority, saying: "My Lord, grant me a kingdom such as belongs to none after me" — by this distinction his rank was elevated above all stars.
And Jesus the physician of healing — understand this — "I revive the dead by the permission of God" — the heart overflows.
All of this derives from the fact that Muhammad is the Seal of Prophecy, yet a Messenger —
The Intercessor of the Prophets, and God's promise to His servant is proclaimed — it belongs to none other.
The Most High calls him a doer of good — by his humanity and purity, a pure and holy Prophet, the home of whom none would bypass —
We settled them and settled the best of believers, and the station of the righteous.
From this station he will be raised — from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, it is well attested:
The trustworthy one said: "I do not worship a Lord whom I have not seen." They said: "Do the eyes see Him?" He replied:
"The eyes did not behold Him directly, but the hearts beheld the depths of gnosis."
The gnostic says in poetry: Where did I first see the face of the Beloved? In Paradise, and the secret was revealed.
O soul, descend — in this world, in the paradise of inner vision, behold the manifestations and acts of worship,
The essence of the Kaaba is this: the purity within, purifying the self, attaining the station
Of witnessing gnosis — to behold the Truth in this world itself; otherwise, Paradise will not be attained.

One can see with the hand of the unseen, and in the grace of the people of the heart, from the purity of the gnostics,
it has been done; the secret of refuge from that era should be understood, turning away from the veil of the world.
Being in the world, necessarily the judgment of existence, "gazing upon its Lord" — gazing from rank and descent,
and rank and vision should be; and the pure spirit of the human soul, the speaking soul,
from the fragrance of God, nourished by sustenance, the sultan with the tongue of the sultanate speaks,
God the Exalted turns toward the elect, and what is devoted to my beloved, my beauty, is described:
"I was the sight of my beloved, established in my heart," he said: "If you see, you act, and you and we recall
and our first and its discourse were of the heart's utterance; from that, its essence was thus:"
Looking inward, in the depth of inquiry, one who truly investigates finds that whoever knows their own soul
has found the capacity of the self and added to it the recognition of the truth of pure essence.
And as much as one performs spiritual discipline, the purity of its essence rises, and by its foundation, it increases further.
And knowledge and gnosis will not remain; as the sun does not remain [hidden] in dryness and cold,
it intercedes and grants grace and abundant mercy to all who are broken,
their deficiencies will vanish; the manifestation of the opening will occur, and they will be sought by it.
And again the possessor of fortune is here, whose happiness in need is real and true,
and the recognition of obligation: a true investigator knows that whatever is destined for humanity
is beyond the contingent; it is with the Necessary Being, or with the contingent being, or with the prevented being —
the prevented being has no need of it, and the contingent being, in all existence,
whatever is other than God — from its nature it originates — as if a relation existed and a connection was established.
And in this path, whoever seeks from the noble ones, the chosen ones, will be informed of the heart's illumination.
The category of contingent being is divided by way of metaphor into two sides: one with knowledge, and
with existence.

Without doubt, with the direction of guidance, on the side of existence, from God, knowledge returns. The existence of form is bound in the world of reference, the attributes of the opposed are established, and the manifest reference continues. It is necessary that the Described One be qualified with attributes essential to the Lord Most High — inevitably, from this, existence is established — and likewise, reason and intellect, contemplation and meaning are founded and secured. They say that what is given no form is established, and the outward name that the attributes wish, together with the attributes — the explanation of their reality comes from our understanding, and the full account is beyond anyone's asking. Praise be — meaning: He transcended description of Himself in truth. The people of the heart said, and the logicians and the Mu'tazilites sought to declare God free of attributes in various ways, disagreeing. Some scholars who were described among them made claims, saying that by their own knowledge and method of transcendence, they afflicted and destroyed some people and called their companions' condition into account — so that the light of divine knowledge, the fruit of transcendence, remained unwitnessed, and guidance was doubtful. "Whomever God guides, none can mislead, and whomever God leads astray, none can guide." And since it became known that all besides God is God's creation, know that every kind has its higher level — and every thousand worlds have one Creator, and that God Most High is, and His essence is Necessarily Existent. Since Necessary Existence is eternal, pre-eternal, without end or cessation, without path to annihilation — and everything other than God, since its existence is originated and contingent, every originated thing admits of beginning, continuation, and passing away. Since no group is the Maker, yet they knew that there exists an eternal, supreme, all-powerful Creator — therefore, by the aid of reason and reflection, a path becomes accessible, and along it one walks rightly and truly.

It was false that they forbade and for every one who knows in a matter that it is false, they should not begin it. And whoever mentions it, contrary to custom, if they themselves engage in corruption of women and lead others astray — as comes in the Noble Word — "For those who turn away, here is the affliction, so beware of them, the alternation of fortune." And upon our fathers and ancestors they would recite, as comes in the saying: "We came to you and our fathers," and "We follow in their footsteps." The Messenger, peace and blessings of God be upon him and his family, forbade following the ways of your fathers and following the ways of the ignorant. Similarly, in the matter of inherited custom and building according to ancient ordinance and military tradition, bounties have fallen away, and in the school of thought there is likewise disagreement. Now, as it is said, the tradition of the Messenger, peace be upon him: "My community will split into seventy-three sects; the one that is saved among them is one, and it is those who follow what I and my companions are upon." Some count the Shia as among the people, and the religion of the Jews is counted among several sects, and the religion of the Christians is included, and so they are honored among them. And these distinctions are obligatory — as it is said, all nations are sought: "From the assembly of words, therein lies the obligation of the companion" — "And in the division of groups, what remains with Abu Bakr" — "And the man and others like him are correct" — "And it was not there, and the flower and the rose, and so on with the wayfarers" — "Two slain ones, and the bodies of the Muslims and the Jews together" — "Those who show the way, bring them" — "The way is known, and consciousness comes alive, and the root grows" — "And they press on in thirst" — "And the multitude of people will come, and the path of the noble" — "And they brought about its truth, and this is not as the Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his family, said: He is the fortunate one from among his community, and the happy one is he who is happy in his mother's womb."

And among the wonders of this world is that in noble discourse it is said that one who seeks in it the way of excellence — the second is contingent happiness, and in comparison to the first it is considered lesser. The happy person is one who, by virtue of righteous deeds and sincere intentions, is of the category of "the servants whose sins are as though they had no sins," for such a one draws near through righteousness, avoids sin, achieves verification of the truth, and attains worldly felicity without falling into ruin. The pillar of felicity is this: that sometimes one sleeps — that is, one rests from action — and sometimes one is awake and engaged in righteous deeds, and from that comes fear and spiritual taste and righteous works increase. One who attains the station of divine nearness receives support and protection, and punishment and torment recede, for deeds are presented before the divine court and one receives their recompense. Know also that sometimes the servant is heedless of the truth for a moment — and on this meaning, the scholar Razi has said that this state is higher than death, for death cuts one off from the world, whereas the death of the creation is in pursuit of the truth and seeking the Lord, as it has been shown that they were created with noble character, and from the divine attributes comes true life, and that paradise is the real one. When the call of remembrance comes to the noble gatherings and assemblies, as the Glorious Word has said: "Say, God," in all aspects — and what the Prophet commanded was: "Take on the character of God," for whoever is aligned with Him in His attributes is like Him in measure, and whoever rises higher in virtue — that is, in the faculty of rational speech and the breaking of the lower self — the purpose is that when the rational soul attains its proper form and goal, union and arrival are achieved. And this is the meaning of what the Most High has said.

Indeed, when We created you for hardship, and since death is inevitable, We have drawn back the veil of mortality — and in that lies richness. By holding to what is proper, living rightly, not dying in the pursuit of worldly gain, and not being among those who merely go through the motions of righteous deeds: this is what is meant. Those who have not performed righteous deeds are, in the reckoning of divine justice, neither truly alive nor truly dead — just as the Quran states: "he shall not die therein, nor live" — meaning whoever is excluded from Paradise is considered to be under punishment, and those in the Fire are rightly so. Such a person is seized by God, for the intellect demands that one reflect carefully.

There are three aspects: first, that a person possesses a rational soul; second, knowledge of the Exalted Truth; third, knowing the religious obligations and sunna regarding food, drink, clothing, and human virtue. One who lacks these qualities truly has no physician to help him, for only the physician of the soul — the true physician — can provide healing. The special qualities and prolonged guidance come from God Almighty, His Prophet, the saints of the faith, and the learned scholars, who are the guides and exemplars. In outward and inward form, this means submitting with great dignity, refraining from boastfulness, being patient, submitting to God's will and pleasure, and accepting His decree — so that the animal faculties, that is, the internal and external senses and appetites, become obedient. The rational soul must then purify itself, come to know the truth, and let the human rational soul guide itself to know who it truly is, where it came from, where it is going, and how to reach the world of the learned by performing righteous deeds. For the purpose of life is to seek goodness — therefore strive to perform righteous deeds.

Among the living of both worlds is the Prophet, our Messenger — may blessings be upon him — who governs outwardly and inwardly. His outward aspect contains the wisdom and judgment derived from the very foundation of justice. The value of the worldly increases, and its inner wisdom encompasses the sustenance of a higher worth. This is because the mercy from above the Throne applies: just as the Messenger said, the Most Merciful grants pardon — meaning that by the measure of the rational faculty, whoever recognizes the origin of their own soul truly stands among the faithful.

Those who seek and desire the other world must first have their worldly concerns settled, then move toward the ultimate end. One must find the guide and ask of the noble teachers. Come, be attentive, descend toward the seeker, be guided and become a messenger. For this reason it is said: "Love of homeland is part of faith," and one of the people of the heart has said:

O heart, turn away from ignorance toward the light of the Holy Spirit, toward its radiance. The Throne is above worldly concerns — remain in the station of that inner fragrance. At this rank, the righteous companion may be found, one who guides the intellect, as has been established, walking the straight path. The soul is purified, the good word rises, as He said: "The good word rises to Him and the righteous deed lifts it." The goal is to gain, through living, what is outwardly and inwardly sound, so that people are held accountable and excused from negligence.

Know that this inward light, even in sleep, advances and prepares the soul. In this quality, those who submit reflect and contemplate deeply. The knowledge of God prevails, and the heart in both sleep and waking is kept with Him. As the Messenger said: "My eyes sleep but my heart does not" — for sleep is the brother of death. Thus one must remember God at all times, and so-called physical death is in truth a glory.

He sang of the eternal life and its manifestation, and described it, which corresponds to what was recorded near Constantinople. The knowledge of revelation has no reward outside of it, just as the Quran reports: "Not even the weight of a particle in the heavens or the earth escapes Him" — and the word "mention" here is used figuratively. This is related to the knowledge of the Creator, and His knowledge is the primordial nature. As much as a person is purified through righteous deeds, they draw closer to perfection. Their acuity will increase and when their ego's selfishness is annihilated, everything other than God becomes forgotten. One must draw near in spirit and station, and when the station of purity is reached, the discourse on unity removes the concerns of duality — seek and you shall find. "Know that God alone is the destroyer of all categories." Therefore the order of mercy is that the truth of Truth is upon the Truth, and this station belongs to the poles of the saints and the great ones. The Messenger made this the foundation, in hearing and in speech and in the foundation of righteous knowledge — in perception and in letters. What was not given and not attained from one's spouse made one greedy, fearful, and abased. Separation, withdrawal, and the subjugation of souls — so that fear and greed fill the heart — and hope does not reach its completion. No rank or station is attained in this way, and no honor or purity is gained. God Almighty has said in the Noble Quran: "He feeds but is not fed." The Sheikh says: So God said: "I made hunger My provision on earth" — and satiety and contentment are the truth, and God Most High says regarding contentment: "Let them eat and enjoy themselves, and let false hope distract them — they will soon know." And whoever accumulates and hoards...

One may attain benefit when one has truly realized every attribute among the attributes of Jund Abu Hali. God the Exalted has said: "Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes Him," and lawful deeds and righteous work arrange the order of humankind. He informs and guides the believers — it is not fitting to seek out wonders by unlawful means or to derive rulings from them. Whoever speaks with sincerity, whoever judges with justice, whoever acts accordingly has established it, and whoever holds fast to it, God guides him to the straight path. He surrendered his life in service, and rarely does one find such perfect conduct and life's full expression. He shows no weariness, and the Prophet also said: "When you rise in the morning, do not burden yourself with matters of loss; and when evening comes, do not burden yourself — wash at dawn and take what sustenance is available to you." Protect yourself from the conceit of rank, and from the arrogance of old age, and be careful not to follow Satan in the pursuit of worldly pleasures and the love of evil. He did not make worship coexist with the worship of Satan. When God most praised sees in these attributes greater effort and desire for knowledge, the angelic attributes increase and the nearness grows. It has been said: "I have no need of this world," and it has established itself as the master. It is great in remembrance and is commanded to glorify. In the Noble Book, the command is given: "Remember God with much remembrance." God the Blessed and Exalted has said: "Remember your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion." We say: Release from the chain of neglect. The remembrance of the Chosen Lord — and our Prophet said: "The best thing given to a human being is a tongue that remembers, a body that is patient, and a heart that is grateful." The verses and reports concerning God's generosity are many in kind; each understanding carries it forward in its own way. The first is the ancient "Allah Hu Hu," which is a great glorification; and the remembrance of His gift is "Haylan Hu."

The first mention is of the tongue: so rightly the remembrance of God, by way of attraction and seclusion, draws one away from ignorance. Through seclusion the purity of all qualities becomes manifest, and by revealing the truth through proof and clear argument, Satan is driven away from the children of Adam, so that he does not become disturbed and distracted from the remembrance of God. "The remembrance of God in the heart drives Satan away as if struck from the side." Therefore, remembrance and reflection is the way, and meditation on the blessings of God Most High — on the physical and spiritual realms and beyond — is the path. Reflection on annihilation leads to the attainment of knowledge, love, and union, ascending through the stations of mystical experience according to one's aspiration for the Truth. At that station, the rank of prophethood descends and returns, and through remembrance one ascends — God grants to each according to their aspiration and effort. Since the road has no end, and the way of the stations is thus, the wayfarer is called to travel it. In the stations of the path, the most correct qualities are said to be: truthfulness, avoidance of falsehood, humility toward people, and showing respect. The meaning of "Glorify God and have compassion for His creation" is to regard all matters of God with great importance, and to look upon all people — common and distinguished alike — with compassion; to show kindness, to treat elders as elders and the young as young; never to envy in any way, and never to belittle anyone who speaks the truth. It is obligatory to maintain good fellowship and connection, to keep away from backbiting and slander, and never to consider oneself superior. It has been said in a verse that the words of our masters and teachers bring blessing to the tongue, and the remembrance of the righteous brings down divine mercy; and one becomes successful before God and before people, and the doors of understanding are opened.

From the presence of divine glory, those who are drawn to it find nearness to the primordial ancient [truth].
When one occupies oneself in calling upon it with sincerity, the greatest gift given is to seek it — as Sufyan [al-Thawri] said:
"O Lord, the remembrance of You suffices me; I have lived and been preserved in life when
You built upon me, O man, one day of grace, and those who required praise — we asked of them the love of beauty."
When love prevails not from within, and from its taste and longing that seeker of truth did not turn,
Because the seeking of love is not possible, and the attainment and union — the forms are sought first;
And every heart in which the inner burning of love is not found remains as if dead and ruled [by heedlessness].
"The first thing God created was the Intellect" — it confers upon the intellect three qualities: the first
Is the knowing of the Truth — that is its weight — the second is the knowing of oneself, the third is the knowing [of others], which is nothing.
Pride entered into the knowing of the Truth and its weight, and it fled from the divine beauty and
Infinite grace. This beauty is firm, and when one came to know oneself, the heart's weight
Is in the certainty of attainment and union — in the majesty of grief is beauty, drawn from within.
Divine beauty was found such that the state and beauty are indistinguishable — without fear and
Love each has its place. The noble ones sought exemption, turning love into a path;
And there is no stability of form, and from the thought of it, beauty arose and returned, and memory
Was established — from non-existence to existence, and from choice they came — and in the world of wonder,
The seekers fly through the realm of grace, passing through the land, so in every movement
They seek the fragrance of Sufyan, and wherever they travel and rest, they yearn for ardent love.
How could the nightingale of the world and the speaker of the capable intellect
Remain without grief within? The heart moved, and the cause of seeking came to it.
And since the soul of man knew of it from those words, it gave itself up like a soul and sea [of longing].

From that union the purpose of both sides was attained, and upon the basis of the manner that has been stated — in verse:
"Had it not been for our nobility, passion would not have come; had it not been for passion, we would not have known — so remember this." And in judgment of this matter it has been said in a couplet:
"Were there love, and were there no lovelessness, then Haydar ibn Nazr would have said: 'If only you knew.'
And there would be a homeland, were the swift one not taken — and were the beautiful one not removed from sight of those who esteem."

On the Chapter of Love: Love, and it is of two kinds — real and metaphorical. Metaphorical love belongs to the world and is attained through hearing and sight, and through the full enjoyment of pleasures and desires.
But true love belongs to the people of realization and those who seek the Lord — it rises from the feet to the heart and is felt within. True love for the people of purity is not attained through hearing and sight, and through the enjoyment of pleasures it does not pass away — it is beyond the kingdom of the world. As it has been said: "Its pleasure is ever-increasing, it is a commotion."
The one with a pure heart attains by means of discipline and remembrance and reflection the state of gnosis.
Servants attain through the perfection of gnosis the station of love; when love reaches its proper place, it becomes —
Love. For they have said: "Love is more than affection, and gnosis increases the pain of longing."
"With us walk two steps toward me and you will have reached the full moon" — and so one attains love.
And it has been said: "Without love nothing is elevated above anything; the mystic who travels by night finds the way."
And love makes a man travel in every path and in every heart it holds a station and a manifestation —
until a prelude appears and through its pages the nightingale and others of that station are reached.
Whoever is not yet entered into the ranks of the elect and the nobility, love has not yet reached him — like the story of Salman.
The call came: "O you who seek the station, enter into its paths, lest Salman and his being be broken."
Especially those who are immersed in outward senses — their inner faculties are spent elsewhere —
They are drawn out from the corner of seclusion until the army of love kills the nightingale — and its note passes on.
And every class, whether in solitude or in populated places, which does not know these things — the source and the existence of being is barred from it.

The seeker strives to find the sought-one, and brings the lover to the beloved, and transforms two separations into union. Just as the Sheikh of Iraq has said: The idol, through its purity —

The cup's subtlety: in every mirror shines the color of the cup of eternity — it is not lacking in anyone.
With the wine of constancy, and the cup of union, and drawing near, seated on the side of love's smoke, which is great — and the tavern's meaning, "idol," is thereby understood.

The narcissus of paradise: they hold a hundred beloved ones for every stranger — O lover, have you yearned?
And the mercy drawn from love is rest and pleasure — the idol: that beloved is not far away.
The one who sits laments: the claimant, if he has proof that love has revealed itself to him — that intoxication is what comes to him,
With blood the nightingale addresses him: when the nightingale laments in blood, the proof of his soul appears — true sincerity
Has no pain. He went away: and it seems the pain of longing was there all along.
The wound cannot be borne from afar, being far from him — I, from near, claim to be freed from it.
He does not scratch it, and those who remain do so through his lament: I see myself fallen, and in his burning lament.

Love, when it reaches the existence of the lover, brings union — its people are made easy and open.
He says: from here, resolve and steadfastness and striving — love says:
From the city of the soul I came, from the abode of the spirit, populated with the blood of my kin, my home and with
The humiliation of my dwelling place, always in distress and commotion, my tears flowing —
A thousand stages through all, so that I do not settle anywhere, and in adversity a thousand gifts.
If I open my lips: if I am Arab in my love, it is an error, and if I am of another tongue, then —
They strike the sky with wonder, and on earth I remain in seclusion and retreat.
In my bewilderment I proceed, and in my clarity, wherever I go I am safe — and if
I turn and lament against the oppressors, even so, though I complain, I remain silent — I am silent.

And with the denial of heat, fleeing from discomfort, heedless, my dwelling has been raised to the heights of grandeur and glory in that court. The seven-knotted structure of the seven heavens stands correct, and my intended destination is refreshed anew. In five degrees of natural craftsmanship, the qualities of my soul rise beyond measure — from this diminution and with this felicity — it is bound, and the whole repeated once more, bringing forth the word of love, established firmly in devotion.

And from among the Arabs, the garment and the bond of attachment spread forth, binding the fine silk upon every side. It has no coral or beryl, yet wherever it attaches itself, the body and its moisture persist. The image of enameled forms is carried away, the mysterious and wondrous is revealed, and the form of humanity is preserved.

The tree called Habb al-Qalb — meaning the "Truffle of the Soul" — in the likeness of the Holy Prophet's form, is the embodiment of thinness and leanness brought forth. When the rational soul, from every side and from every direction, renews the green meadow in the shadow of the kingdoms, and every compounded essence stands correct in its state — henna and care are given — it is said that wherever such things are brought into use, the custom of clay is maintained. And every perfect soul that descends into the form of leanness brings forth the beauty of those of noble character.

The verse says: "They say: the pure reckoning and the clear statement" — mirror of the heart, the taste of love contradicts their nature, and the natural repeller causes suffering. That tree, with the keepers of its orchards, from the spring of souls, was not to be found. The one acquainted with it perishes, and we diminish it; its difference comes and goes. In the hearts of loved ones and rivals, in the hearts of all servants, from the idols of the homeland — knowing how — and from shame and bewilderment, from head to foot wrapped in it, humble and light, the soul rises up in spirit.

The preservation and sustaining of this world in both its visible and hidden dimensions is kept together, and the physician and every physician has read and attained a station in knowledge before the sovereign, firmly established, so that the state of the age has become known by name and renown. It has become established in the school of thought, though in appearance they are all humans. In that long road, this noble station is achieved perhaps once in a thousand by those devoted, and from the prophets those who attain it — aside from the agreed-upon and mentioned — the path is not reached. For years one must endure until the original ruby stone brings forth its brilliance and grants its gifts. Every witness to this recognizes that one must depend on divine accord and assistance, so that ease may be achieved. May the blessings of God be upon him, and God — without God we would not be guided, and we would not be truthful, and we would not be upright. Glorified is He, and He says: thus we seek from Him guidance and the gift of His grace and generosity and favor. The qualities of motion are such that the human being possesses them as a trust. It is wondrous that the qualities of the human are gathered, and for this reason, in the meadow of humanity, the treasury is measured, and in the realm of reason and the qualities of humanity, they descend from the lineage of Adam. Bringing forth their humanity in proper letters is fitting, and it is for this reason that the Book of Wonders was composed — to bring benefit to people from the wonders gathered therein, of beauty and grace, to be a guide and an aid, so that among all the descendants of Adam none may say they were left without guidance, that they may rise and build and extend their hands to support one another.

It does not reach [them], and people, for the protection of their offspring, make attacks, and their daughters are taken in marriage. They keep count of this, and the care of their children is never neglected. Most often if their children show affection, it is rare that they cover themselves with clothing made of skin. Their cleverness in recognizing plants is at its utmost, and people take their due from them and benefit from them and show them affection, and by gestures they make themselves understood. Their children they raise as their own, and it is remarkable how their wild offspring attach themselves with affection to their own kind, though tame ones feel attached by heart.

In the Book of Wonders [Ajaib al-Makhluqat] it is mentioned that in the great sea there are creatures who make a great noise, and their faces and minds are oriented toward good, and their limbs are mostly like those of humans; they can speak, and some of them have been seen among people appearing human in form. Their intelligence surpasses by degrees that of a young Cancer-born [creature]; their bodies have been adorned. They are such that their majority is remarkable; they are incomparable to those of the land; they are a kind of sea-creature [deval]. Among them are stories of ancient peoples that are told of the great sea, and in between them are human-like forms without spines, and they are somehow satisfied among themselves.

In the Book of Wonders it says that a people, when spoken to, do not respond but strike [with their bodies], and they torment those who encounter them. And this is such a weak thing that if someone causes a death, hanging by the feet would be [their punishment], and death comes upon them. They are tamed like trained animals that remain, and they are smooth, and they go upon the mountain. The true picture of the Deval is painted thus, and its nature is thus described, and the voice it makes is known. It does not reach [further]; the account of the Deval: its examination is as described — this treatise, and from this...

The name of the idol Wal: they call it Atquma, and the idol is like a standing figure, known as Nasil or Kuya. It is mentioned in the book Ajaib al-Makhluqat that in the islands of the Sea of China there are groups of red-faced peoples, and their stature is four spans tall, and they are speaking beings; they have been known from ancient times. They go about and communicate with one another and trade and barter goods. In exchange they are content, and in the islands of the sea there are groups whose stature matches their own. They send among themselves, every year to every market, and they bring goods to the markets, and the merchants exchange with them. It is mentioned in Ajaib al-Makhluqat that they are called Kalm Kus. Among the blessings assigned to them is that they live near Gog and Magog, and they dwell in the mountains. They are called by the great name and they are reckoned among the people of that region by the reckoning of Dawud and Ibn Amir. It is reported that Sipahr, son of Noah's servant, Hiflan, was one of them, and their settlements are in the region of Adabkiyya. From their stature they are called Kalm Kus, and they have been given this name as an appellation. The author of the book Ajaib al-Makhluqat, when he mentions them together with the Kalm, verifies this and records it, and says that the greater part of the inhabited region in the time of the Mongols is such, and many of them have honored the religion of Islam. Their king submitted and ruled over the peoples of that land, and the princes and commanders of the country came and were obedient, occupying themselves with worship and devotion, and seeking the highest aspirations. They surpassed the people of their time, and the Kalm Kus groups were depicted in the form described by the author of Ajaib al-Makhluqat, as the progeny of Qasil son of Adam, as mentioned therein.

They are found in the eastern boundaries. The people called "Mardumkhar" live in the islands of China and Zanzibar. They are dark-faced and powerfully built, in strength like the Mardumkhar. They know of no civilization and live in islands, dwelling in the forests, sustaining themselves and living off the flesh of men. They pay no attention to other foods. In the Wonders of Strange Things it is said that the islands of China are peoples cut off by an arm of the sea, divided into halves — Adishanazamat, Nimsarwabalt, Kusn, Balthaysam, Balitnimu, and Bakis — and Bakiya and Baln, each named after a people known as the people of wind, who are heard of in those lands. In the Book of Peoples it is written that these groups were sent down from the lineage of Abareen, in the name of Barnam, son of Noah, peace be upon him, and it is said that their name traces back to Tamsinidad ibn Nughad, meaning "son of Noah," and in the book of creatures and animals of Moses, peace be upon him, and in the Compendium of Anecdotes it is written that the origin of these peoples was Arab, and they were transformed in form, and from that people those who are in intellect and nature like Gog and Magog — meaning the scholars say they descend from the lineage of Cain, son of Adam — and it is also said their line comes from Kawsidan Nazar, Awarkhan ibn Qaraqhan ibn Masnak, and Halabat ibn Barqawa ibn Yafeth ibn Noah, peace be upon him. Since these peoples were exceedingly numerous and half of them devastated the lands, the inhabitants of those regions and territories sought to repel them and erected a barrier. Then Dhu al-Qarnayn came and built a great barrier against them and repelled them. The Glorious Word of God reports: "Until when he reached the place between the two mountains, he found beside them a people who could scarcely understand any speech. They said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land, so shall we make for you payment that you might make between us and them a barrier? He said: That in which my Lord has established me is better, so assist me with strength."

He placed between you and them a firm barrier of iron, until when it leveled off between the two walls — and the promise of my Lord was true. And the people of that time ran forth from it.

In the last age, near the appearance of the Day of Resurrection, they will emerge. And the signs of the approach of the Hour are that they are great in stature and large in build. Their provisions come from trees of the mountains, sable, and well-known fish. Some of them resemble in form fine trees, cypress, and named varieties.

The Third Discourse: On the Description of Faith, Sanctified Places, and Holy Sites — and these are four chapters.

The First Chapter: On the mention of the Two Noble Sanctuaries — may God Most High ennoble them — and the intention behind affirming faith in them, seeking blessing and auspiciousness. Mentioning them first is fitting before speaking of faith, and in reference to a noble passage in the Holy Quran and Hadith: the word of God Most High: "Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him some of Our signs. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing." And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "No journey is undertaken to three mosques" — the Sacred Mosque, the Farthest Mosque, and this Mosque, which is the House of the Kaaba.

The Sacred Mosque is in the city of Mecca. This sanctuary is at the center of the world. On one side are Abu Qubays and the mountains, and on the other side are the mountains of Mina and the hills of Muzdalifah, where the sacrificial ram of Ishmael descended. And it is the place where Abraham spoke and sought the dinar, as prompted by the word of God Most High: "When Abraham said: My Lord, make this city secure" — and the Messenger of God said: "This city was made sacred by God on the day He created the heavens and the earth; it is sacred by His decree and ordinance." No sin is to be committed within it, and mention should be made that it is the origin of all good.

The regions and surroundings of al-Karzaz and the districts of Ta'if are like paradise, elevated above Mecca. Ta'if is known for this reason: it is pleasant, and Ta'if is near the mountain of Arafat, where snow and ice are found, unlike anywhere else in the Arab lands.
